Description: WS2812B is the protocol underpinning Klipper LED integration across the self-build ecosystem. The Stealthburner logo LED and disco LED mounts are built around it, and the Voron configuration macro library provides STATUS_PRINTING, STATUS_HEATING, STATUS_ERROR, and STATUS_COMPLETE effects out of the box. For anything beyond basic on/off enclosure lighting — print state feedback, animations, idle indicators — WS2812B is the starting point. Use RGBW variants (SK6812) if you need accurate white output for print monitoring.
Verdict Label: Stealthburner logo and Klipper effects standard — native [neopixel] support in Klipper, extensive community macro library
Name: WS2812B Neopixel LED Strip
Pros:
Individually addressable RGB — each LED is independently controllable for print status effects and animations
Native Klipper [neopixel] configuration support — STATUS_PRINTING, STATUS_HEATING, STATUS_ERROR macros are pre-built in Voron configs
Stealthburner logo and disco LED integrations are designed specifically around WS2812B protocol
5V signal from most toolboards works without level shifting
Community macro library is extensive — Voron-owned macros, Ellis config, and third-party packages all support WS2812B
Cons:
5V over long runs (2m+) causes voltage drop — power injection at strip intervals is required for consistent color at far ends
Heat sensitivity — WS2812B ICs degrade above ~60°C, limiting direct placement inside hot chamber environments
Data signal degrades over long cable runs — a 330Ω series resistor on the data line is community-standard practice
Cannot produce neutral white light — RGB mixing always has a color cast; not ideal as primary print illumination without RGBW variants

Description: COB LED strips at 24V are the practical first choice for enclosure lighting on self-build printers. Running directly from the printer's main PSU, they need no separate power supply and connect with two wires to any spare output. COB technology produces even, diffused illumination — better for print monitoring than individual-dot strips. They're not addressable and can't integrate with Klipper LED macros, but for the purpose of seeing inside your printer clearly, nothing matches COB strips for simplicity and value.
Verdict Label: Simplest enclosure lighting upgrade — runs from the 24V printer PSU, even illumination, no controller needed
Name: COB LED Strip 24V White
Pros:
Runs directly from the printer's 24V PSU — no separate power supply, tap into existing wiring
COB (Chip on Board) technology produces uniform, diffused light with no hot spots — better for print monitoring photography than dot-matrix strips
Simple two-wire installation — connect to a spare fan output for PWM dimming, or a MOSFET board
High CRI (90+) options available at low cost — important for accurate color in print monitoring or video
Very high lumen output per dollar compared to individual LED strips
Cons:
Not addressable — cannot create lighting effects or integrate with Klipper LED status macros
Always-on unless wired to a PWM-capable output or relay — basic installations run at full brightness constantly
24V COB variants are less common than 12V — verify voltage spec carefully before ordering from AliExpress listings
High-density COB strips generate some heat — factor into enclosure thermal design for small chambers

Description: A 10-LED strip of SK6812 RGBCW addressable LEDs, sold by Fabreeko for $3.99. Each pixel carries red, green, blue and a dedicated cool-white LED, so it produces accurate white light for print monitoring where plain RGB strips always have a colour cast. It runs on 5V and speaks the same single-wire protocol as WS2812B, so Klipper drives it natively with [neopixel] using color_order GRBW. Best suited to toolhead accents, logo lighting and short status strips rather than full enclosure illumination.
Verdict Label: RGBW neopixel strip with a real cool-white channel — accurate white for print monitoring, native Klipper [neopixel] support
Name: SK6812 RGBCW
Pros:
Individually addressable RGB + dedicated cool-white channel — true white without the RGB-mix colour cast, ideal for print monitoring
Native Klipper [neopixel] support — configure with color_order GRBW, works with Voron status macros
Only $3.99 for a 10-LED strip — cheapest way to add accurate-white lighting
Same WS2812B-compatible single-wire data protocol — daisy-chains with existing neopixel setups
Cons:
5V over long runs causes voltage drop — power injection needed for longer strips
SK6812 ICs degrade above ~60°C — keep out of the hottest chamber spots
Only 10 LEDs in this Fabreeko strip — enough for a logo or toolhead accent, not full enclosure lighting
Data signal degrades over long cable runs — series resistor on the data line is community-standard practice

Description: WLED running on an ESP32 (available pre-flashed from Athom) is the community's preferred approach for standalone addressable LED control on 3D printers. The Moonraker integration plugin allows Klipper to push print state changes directly to WLED, triggering effects on print start, heating, completion, and error without modifying Klipper macros. It supports virtually all common addressable strip types and can be controlled from any browser. The trade-off vs. direct Klipper [neopixel] is added network complexity, but the benefit is richer effects and independence from the Klipper restart cycle.
Verdict Label: Go-to standalone LED controller for Voron lighting — Moonraker plugin integrates WLED effects with Klipper print state
Name: WLED Controller
Pros:
WLED firmware on ESP32 supports WS2812B, SK6812 (RGBW), WS2815 (12V), and many other addressable strip types
Moonraker plugin links Klipper print state to WLED effects — print start, heating, complete, and error states trigger LED changes automatically
Web UI, HTTP API, MQTT, and WebSocket control — integrates into Home Assistant, Homebridge, or custom dashboards
Pre-flashed Athom units available — plug-and-play, no soldering or firmware flashing required
Decouples LED control from the Klipper host — LED strips stay on during Klipper restarts or updates
Cons:
Requires WiFi access inside the printer chassis — signal strength can be marginal inside fully metal enclosures
Moonraker plugin requires manual installation and configuration — not zero-config
Adds a network device to your setup — more complexity vs. direct Klipper GPIO neopixel control
WLED configuration has a learning curve for users new to home automation-style tools

Description: The Raspberry Pi Camera v3 Wide is the community's default recommendation for Klipper print monitoring. Its 12MP IMX708 sensor and 120° wide-angle optic cover the full build area of enclosed printers in a single frame, while the CSI interface integrates directly with Crowsnest without driver configuration. Phase-detection autofocus means you mount it once and forget the focus. The only hard constraint is Raspberry Pi host dependency — if your build runs a CB1 or other SBC, verify libcamera support before ordering.
Verdict Label: Community top pick for Klipper — CSI interface, 12MP, Crowsnest native, autofocus out of the box
Name: Camera v3 Wide
Pros:
12MP IMX708 sensor — sharp, low-noise output for print monitoring and timelapse
120° wide FOV covers the full build area of an enclosed printer without corner mounting
CSI connection to the Pi host — no USB bandwidth competition with host controllers or Manta
Crowsnest natively supports Pi Camera v3 — zero-config setup, no manual stream driver installation
Phase-detection autofocus — adapts automatically to different camera positions without manual tuning
Best image quality per dollar in the Klipper camera ecosystem
Cons:
CSI ribbon cable is limited in length — typically 30cm stock, up to ~1m with quality flex cables before signal degradation; long runs inside enclosures require care
Requires a Raspberry Pi host — does not work with Raspberry Pi alternatives (CB1, BTT Manta SBC mode) unless using libcamera-compatible OS
Camera cable routing inside a hot enclosed printer can stress the ribbon connector

Description: The Kirigami UFO is livinhack's UFO-edition variant of the Kirigami PCB mod: two PCBs (Frame PCB and Kirigami PCB) that tidy the wiring of a Voron V0.1/V0.2 Kirigami bed into a single 10-pin Micro-Fit harness, breaking out the heater, bed fan and neopixel connections at the bed. The set includes the Molex and XH pins; all other parts come from the GitHub BOM, and the bed fan and front neopixel are optional extras, not included. It is a wiring breakout first and a lighting product only in that the Frame PCB loops the neopixel signal through.
Verdict Label: V0 Kirigami bed wiring breakout — tidies bed wiring into one 10-pin harness, with neopixel loop-through
Name: Kirigami UFO
Pros:
Combines all bed wiring into a single 10-pin Micro-Fit 3.0 harness — much tidier than loose wires on a V0 Kirigami bed
Breaks out heater, bed fan and neopixel connections at the bed itself for easy service
Neopixel loop-through on the Frame PCB keeps front status LEDs working
Optional bed fan and Kirigami front supported from the same PCBs
Cons:
Voron V0.1/V0.2 Kirigami bed only — useless on any other printer
No LEDs included — the lighting is only a pass-through; the front neopixel is a separate part
Requires Molex/XH crimping and the rest of the BOM from GitHub — not a plug-and-play kit
$39.99 buys two bare PCBs plus pins; printed parts and all other components are sourced separately

Description: Voron Daylight on a Stick is a 24V LED bar by Bartlammers (Blamm) that mounts to 2020 extrusion to light the print chamber. It runs at 24V from the main PSU and needs no separate power management. The bar format spreads bright white light across the build area, making it easy to see prints in progress. Not addressable — chamber lighting is about illumination, not effects.
Verdict Label: Community-designed compact 24V toolhead LED PCB — the standard lighting solution for Stealthburner and AfterBurner
Name: Daylight on a Stick
Pros:
Community-designed PCB purpose-built for Voron toolhead mounting — dimensions match Stealthburner and AfterBurner mounts
Runs at 24V from the printer PSU — no separate voltage regulation or power supply
Compact stick-format PCB keeps the light source as close to the nozzle as possible without interfering with print cooling
High CRI daylight-white LEDs — neutral, accurate illumination for toolhead-level print monitoring and photography
LDO Voron kits include Daylight on a Stick by default — if you're buying a Voron kit, you likely already have these
Cons:
Not addressable — on/off or PWM dimming only; no RGB effects or Klipper color macros
Voron-specific dimensions — mounting on non-Voron toolheads requires community-adapted mount designs
Requires PWM-capable output or manual wiring for dimming; basic installations run at constant brightness
Not stocked at all vendors — availability tied to Voron kit restocks from LDO, Formbot, and similar

Description: The nozzle camera is a category of community mods rather than a specific product — builders mount inexpensive USB macro cameras at toolhead level to observe the nozzle and first layer in real time. When paired with Obico or a Klipper camera stream, this enables early failure detection and diagnostics that a standard overhead camera cannot provide. The limiting factor is standardization: mounting solutions, heat shielding, and camera selection are all builder-specific, and community consensus on a recommended solution hasn't solidified.
Verdict Label: Emerging community mod category — nozzle-level inspection adds real diagnostic value but no production-ready solution exists yet
Name: Nozzle Camera
Pros:
Real-time nozzle-level inspection — enables early identification of first-layer adhesion issues, partial clogs, and stringing before they cause print failures
Low component cost — generic USB macro cameras work for this purpose
Compatible with Obico (formerly Spaghetti Detective) for AI-assisted failure detection
Community-designed mounts exist for Stealthburner and similar toolheads
Cons:
No standardized production mount — each implementation is builder-specific (Voron Discord threads, GitHub, Printables)
Extreme heat proximity to the nozzle degrades camera optics and sensor lifespan — heat shielding and careful positioning are required
Calibration and framing are finicky — small positioning errors change what the camera captures significantly
No polished plug-and-play solution yet — this is a hobbyist frontier, not a finished product category

Description: Dr. Dave's Disco Skirts are a pair of WS2812B addressable RGB LED boards that mount in the skirts between the fans on the sides of a Voron, adding colour effects where a normal strip cannot fit. The $26.99 Fabreeko listing is a set of two boards and includes two diffusers; printed parts come from the GitHub repo. The design is a reshaped copy of Blamm's Disco on a Stick, so it wires and configures the same way — 5V, single data line, Klipper [neopixel]. Decorative only: it is bling, not chamber lighting.
Verdict Label: Decorative WS2812B skirt lighting for Voron — pure bling, Klipper neopixel-driven, with diffusers included
Name: Disco Skirts
Pros:
Individually addressable WS2812B LEDs — full RGB effects via Klipper [neopixel] and the led_effect plugin
Set of 2 with 2 diffusers included — one for each side skirt
Open design on GitHub, derived from Blamm's documented Disco on a Stick
Fits the skirts between the side fans — lighting where a strip cannot go
Cons:
Purely cosmetic — adds no print illumination or monitoring value
Printed parts required from GitHub, not included in the $26.99 set
Minimal documentation — the author calls it "a silly board" and notes he spent no time documenting it; Blamm's Disco on a Stick docs are the reference
Needs a spare 5V neopixel output and data line — 5V, not the printer's 24V rail

Description: The Logitech C920 is the default recommendation for Klipper users who aren't running a Raspberry Pi host, or who want USB simplicity over CSI performance. It's extensively documented in Crowsnest and works reliably across all SBC types. The trade-offs vs. Pi Camera v3 are real — 78° FOV, lower resolution, and a higher price — but for builds running anything other than an RPi, it's the straightforward choice.
Verdict Label: Reliable USB timelapse classic — works with any Klipper host but image quality and FOV lag behind Pi Camera v3
Name: C920 HD Webcam
Pros:
USB plug-and-play — works with any Klipper host (Pi, CB1, BTT Manta SBC, BIGTREETECH Pi) regardless of SBC type
Extensively documented in Crowsnest — widely deployed, dozens of working Klipper config examples
H.264 hardware encoding onboard — lower CPU load on the host vs. MJPEG software encoding
Broad retail availability — from electronics stores, not just 3D printing vendors
Cons:
78° FOV is noticeably narrower than the Pi Camera v3 Wide — may miss corners on larger enclosed builds without repositioning
Autofocus less reliable for close-distance enclosure mounting — manual focus lock mod often recommended by the community
USB competes for bandwidth on the same host hub as the Klipper USB connection
Higher price than Pi Camera v3 for lower resolution and narrower FOV in this context

Description: LED status boards for the ERCF v2 (Enraged Rabbit Carrot Feeder), sold as the 4-light Carrot on a Stick and the 2-light Carrot on a Twig. The boards carry WS2812 addressable LEDs that Happy Hare drives as per-gate status indicators, so each filament lane shows its load state at a glance. A collaboration between XR Bunker and Fabreeko for the ERCF community.
Verdict Label: ERCF v2 status LEDs — per-gate neopixel feedback via Happy Hare, bling with a purpose
Name: Carrot on a Stick & Carrot on a Twig
Pros:
Per-gate status LEDs driven by Happy Hare — see which filament lane is loaded at a glance
WS2812 addressable LEDs integrate with Klipper [neopixel] — colour and effects follow print/MMU state
Two sizes cover small and large ERCF builds (2-light Twig, 4-light Stick)
Purpose-built PCB for ERCF v2, no DIY strip wiring
Cons:
ERCF v2 only — useless without the Enraged Rabbit feeder
Fabreeko's own page carries almost no documentation ("more info to be released soon")
Optional bling — the ERCF works fine without it
Two variants share one listing, so the price depends on which board you pick

Description: Remix of the front bed-mount light for the Voron V0.2 Kirigami bed, by Shammy. A single addressable neopixel on a small PCB with PH connectors, plus a breakout board with Wago connectors for tool-free wiring; wire is not included. It gives the V0.2 a Klipper-driven status light at the front of the bed.
Verdict Label: V0.2 Kirigami bed status light — single neopixel, PH + Wago connectors, no soldering
Name: Kirigami LED and Breakout — V0.2
Pros:
Purpose-built front light for the V0.2 Kirigami bed — bolts straight on
Single addressable neopixel gives Klipper status colours from the front of the printer
PH connectors plus Wago breakout — no soldering, tool-free wiring
Cheap status-light upgrade for a V0.2 build
Cons:
V0.2 Kirigami bed only — no use on any other printer
Wire not included, despite the breakout needing it
Single LED only — a status indicator, not enclosure lighting
Thin documentation — Fabreeko lists the remix with no wiring diagram

Description: The UV version of Blamm's Daylight on a Stick: a 270mm, 24V LED bar for Voron printers 250mm and up, using UV LEDs instead of white daylight LEDs. It makes fluorescent and UV-reactive printed parts glow inside the enclosure, and mounts to 2020 extrusion with the same printed brackets as the Daylight family. It is effect lighting, not general illumination — it will not help you see print colours accurately.
Verdict Label: UV effect bar for fluorescent parts — same 24V Daylight design, but no use as general lighting
Name: Nightlight on a Stick
Color Temp (K): UV — no color temperature (ultraviolet, not white light)
Pros:
UV LEDs make fluorescent and UV-reactive parts glow — a fun effect no white bar can do
Same 24V Daylight-family design — runs from the printer PSU, mounts to 2020 extrusion with standard printed brackets
270mm length suits 250mm-and-up Vorons
Simple on/off or PWM dimming via a spare heater output
Cons:
UV only — useless as general print lighting and distorts print colours
Not addressable — no RGB effects or Klipper colour macros
UV wavelength is not published, so the exact fluorescence response is unverified
Single-purpose effect bar at the same price as the white Daylight bar

Description: A set of four WS2812 3535 RGB sequin LEDs sized for the Voron Mini Stealthburner (11 × 5 mm, ~2 mm thick), based on a Lab4450 design and sold by FYSETC. It ships with 1 m of 26 AWG Teflon wire for installation in the Mini SB nozzle and logo positions. Each LED is individually addressable through Klipper's [neopixel] section, so it works with the standard Voron status macros for print state feedback.
Verdict Label: Standard Mini Stealthburner nozzle/logo LEDs — 4x WS2812 sequins with 1 m wire, native Klipper [neopixel] support
Name: Sequins RGB WS2812 for Mini SB
Pros:
4 individually addressable WS2812 RGB LEDs — full Klipper [neopixel] status effects and animations
Sized for the Mini Stealthburner nozzle and logo positions, with 1 m Teflon wire included
5V single-wire data — plugs into the standard neopixel output on toolhead boards
$5.99 for the set — the cheapest way to add status lighting to a V0/Mini SB build
Cons:
RGB only — cannot produce neutral white light for print illumination
Tiny 11 × 5 mm boards need soldering and careful wire routing inside the toolhead
5V WS2812 ICs are heat-sensitive — keep away from the hotend/heater block

Description: A kit of four LDO-made WS2812 RGB LED PCBs with pre-terminated cables, one per BoxTurtle lane, that daisy-chain into a single Klipper neopixel chain. The LEDs give per-lane status feedback through Happy Hare / the AFC Klipper Add-On (ready, loading, fault), so you can see at a glance which lane is active. It is compatible with all BoxTurtle builds and connects to the ARGB LED outputs on the AFC-Lite/AFC-Pro controller.
Verdict Label: Official LDO lane-indicator kit for BoxTurtle — 4 WS2812 PCBs with pre-terminated cables, driven as a Klipper neopixel chain
Name: LED PCB and Cables for BoxTurtle
Pros:
4 WS2812 PCBs + pre-terminated cables included — no soldering, one PCB per lane
Per-lane status feedback in Klipper via Happy Hare / AFC neopixel support
Manufactured by LDO, made for the BoxTurtle — mounting and wiring match the official docs
5V ARGB from the controller's buck converter — no separate PSU or level shifting
Cons:
BoxTurtle-only — useless without an Armored Turtle AFC build
Currently out of stock at Fabreeko (as of 2026-11-15) — check before ordering
Only 4 LEDs — lane indicators, not enclosure illumination
Needs the LED Effects / Happy Hare neopixel config to do more than static colours

Description: The Glow Stick is the UV version of Blamm's Daylight on a Matchstick — a short 157 mm LED bar sized for V0 printers, running at 24V straight from the printer PSU. Instead of white light it emits UV, so it is for glow effects and UV-reactive prints rather than seeing inside the chamber. Printed mounts are available from the Voron-Hardware Daylight repo on GitHub.
Verdict Label: UV version of the Daylight Matchstick for V0 — 157 mm, 24V, for glow effects rather than general illumination
Name: Glow Stick
Color Temp (K): UV — no color temperature (ultraviolet, not white light)
Pros:
UV light bar purpose-built for V0-sized printers (157 mm)
24V, two-wire — runs from the printer PSU, no separate supply or controller
Same proven Matchstick/Daylight PCB family by Blamm, with printed mounts on GitHub
Cheap accent lighting at $19.99
Cons:
UV only — useless as general chamber illumination; you still need a white light for print monitoring
Not addressable — on/off or PWM dimming only, no effects or Klipper colour macros
V0 short length — too short for 2.4/Trident chambers (the Nightlight on a Stick is the full-size UV equivalent)
UV wavelength is unpublished — no nm figure on the Fabreeko page or in the repo
